# The `pkli` command line

`pkli` is one binary with a verb per job. This page is its reference.

## Usage

The block below is the text `pkli` prints for a usage error, rendered from
the binary's own source by `pklith-dev cli`; the `cli-doc` step fails when
the two differ.

<!-- BEGIN usage: generated by `cargo run -p pklith-dev -- cli` from pkli's usage text; do not edit -->
```text
usage: pkli <command> | --version

  check [--root DIR] [--registry FILE] [--staged | --range A..B]
                                         every tracked file has a type in .pklith with its checks;
                                         --staged: only what the commit changes; a diff feeds `changed` rules
  confirm                                accept the gate: complete, faithful, runnable, deterministic
  detect [--root DIR] [--registry FILE]  the fragments the tracked files switch on, one per line
  gen [--check]                          write hk.pklith.pkl from .pklith; --check: fail when it is stale
  lay [--dry-run]                        one commit per missing check, through the hooks; --dry-run: list them
  map [--staged | FILE...]               the specs covering a change, one per line; exit 1 when one is missing
  migrate [--drop ID,...]                a lefthook repo onto hk, only if every check survives
  protect [--dry-run] [--repo O/N] [--branch B] [--accept-removals]
                                         branch protection's required contexts from CI jobs, through gh (network)
  report [--format text|json|md]         the coverage matrix and findings, always printed; takes --root, --registry
  seed [--init]                          write the seed files the fragments ask for, never over one; --init: and a first .pklith
  import DOC                             a .pklith from a legacy linter coverage document, on stdout
```
<!-- END usage -->

`pkli --version` prints the crate version and the built-in catalog's
fingerprint, which changes exactly when the catalog does.

## Behaviour every verb shares

- **Exit codes**: 0 when all is well, 1 for a finding (a gap, drift, a
  missing spec), 2 for a usage error or anything that could not be read or
  run. A verb that could not do its job never exits 0.
- **Streams**: stdout carries data only (a list, a report, a registry);
  every finding and diagnostic goes to stderr, so output can be piped.
- **Where it runs**: from any subdirectory, `pkli` acts on the repository
  root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`); `--root DIR` names another tree.
  Outside a repository without `--root`, it exits 2.
- **Paths**: a path argument is always opened as a path, never read as a
  flag, even when it starts with `-`.
- **Network**: only `pkli protect` reaches it, through `gh`, and only when
  you run it.

## Installed under another name

`packages.compat` installs `pkli` as `lefthook-linter-coverage`,
`lefthook-linter-coverage-full` and `lefthook-unit-coverage`. Under those
names it ignores its arguments and behaves as the legacy tool: the same
environment variables, messages and exit codes, with the deliberate
differences listed in [`src/legacy/SPEC.md`](../src/legacy/SPEC.md).
